thread:
Ava (CEO): quick follow-up from today's AM all-hands: we got good questions about positioning. i want a short doc that makes clear who we9re winning for and why.
Sam (VP Product): agree. propose a 1-pager: target customer personas (ai-native, platform teams), top pain they solve (unpredictable inference economics), and 3 proof points.
Jordan (Sales): from field: each persona speaks different language. AE needs 2-3 battlecards: one for cost-conscious infra leads, one for security/compliance buyers, one for product teams looking for low-latency.
Priya (Head of Research): research can supply benchmark artifacts and qualitative notes on where open models + our runtime beat other stacks. will include caveats about dataset and sequence-length differences.
Mira (Eng): we should standardize the perf artifacts. suggest a template: workload description, p50/p95/p99, batch size, model variant, hardware. easy to reproduce.
Leo (SRE): also include failure modes and fallback behavior in the demo bundles. customers ask about "what happens when a node flaps".
Ava (CEO): yes. one message from me: our core claim should be compact and defensible: "Predictable and economical inference across deployment modes." avoid long lists.
Sam (VP Product): can we map that claim to 3 measurable tests that product/eng can own this quarter?
Priya (Head of Research): suggested tests: 1) 20% reduction in median token cost for typical PLG workload after recommended batch/caching settings, 2) p99 < 500ms for 90% of production-like requests at target load, 3) conversion rate from trial -> dedicated >= 5% for qualifying accounts.
Jordan (Sales): are those targets realistic? sales needs something we can promise in conversations.
Mira (Eng): we can aim for the p99 target on our curated models + optimized kernels. need to instrument more tail latency signals across regions.
Leo (SRE): note: multi-region failover testing requires a scheduled DR run. put it on eng-sre calendar.
Ava (CEO): good. next: competitors. we9re hearing three themes in competitor messaging: cheaper at scale, single-tenant performance, and more integrations. we should rebut with clear artifacts, not FUD.
Priya (Head of Research): i'll produce a short competitive matrix with signal sources and recommended benchmarks. will also flag claims that are marketing-only.
Sam (VP Product): product will convert that into two short customer-facing pages: "When to pick Redwood" and "When to pick self-host". keep it honest.
Jordan (Sales): can we get TL;DR lines for the AE playbook? one-liners for rebuttals.
Mira (Eng): engineering will provide sample p99 charts and a simple script to re-run the benchmark.
Ava (CEO): timeline: 2 weeks for internal artifacts, 4 weeks for customer-ready decks. owners: Sam (product) leads artifacts; Priya (research) owns benchmarks; Jordan (sales) owns AE collateral; Mira (eng) and Leo (sre) produce reproducible artifacts.
Sam (VP Product): noted. i'll post the owner doc with dates after this thread.
Priya (Head of Research): small ask: can we get a single source of truth for benchmark configs? a repo or a doc-bot entry?
doc-bot: (system) New doc template created: "benchmarks/standard-config.md" -> /docs/internal/benchmarks
Mira (Eng): i'll sync with Priya to move example infra into a reproducible folder.
Jordan (Sales): i'll gather top 10 buyer objections and post by EOD Fri.
Ava (CEO): final: keep customer stories front and center. numbers matter, but short narratives about how we saved cost or simplified rollout win rooms.
Leo (SRE): scheduling note: plan a DR/failover test next month. will propose dates in eng-sre.
Sam (VP Product): thanks all. follow-up will have owners and deadlines.
Ava (CEO): thanks everyone 91
